title: Cajón del Maipo
slogan: Up the Maipo out of Santiago into the high Andes: gorge, then desert, then glaciers at the end of the tarmac.

waypoints.name: San Alfonso

waypoints.name: El Volcán
waypoints.advice: 79 km in you reach El Volcán. The road climbs 300 m over the 40 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 3 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Baños Morales, 39 km on and climbing 400 m.

waypoints.name: Baños Morales
waypoints.advice: Baños Morales closes the day. The road climbs 400 m over the 39 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 5 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher.

scenicChapters.title: Cajón del Maipo
scenicChapters.narrative: For 45 km this is Cajón del Maipo, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Cajón del Maipo
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 36 km. 400 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

title: Portillo and Los Libertadores
slogan: The old road to Argentina: thirty numbered hairpins stacked up the Caracoles to three thousand metres.

waypoints.name: Los Andes
waypoints.advice: Los Andes is where the day begins. Next is Río Blanco, 32 km on and climbing 600 m.

waypoints.name: Río Blanco

waypoints.name: Portillo
waypoints.advice: 64 km in you reach Portillo. The road climbs 1460 m over the 32 km before it, hard. Reckon on about 13 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Caracoles, 32 km on and climbing 320 m.

waypoints.name: Caracoles
waypoints.advice: The high point of this section, 3200 m up. The road climbs 320 m over the 32 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 15 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October.

scenicChapters.title: Los Andes → Río Blanco
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 56 km. 600 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Paso de los Libertadores
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 6.7%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.

scenicChapters.title: Paso de los Libertadores
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 3200 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

title: Valparaíso Coast Road
